questions.text: Explain Rani Abbakka Devi's struggle against the Portuguese in the defense of Ullal.
questions.text_as_printed: Explain Rani Abbakka Devi's struggle against the Portuguese in the defense of Ullal. (Average )

answer.value: In A.D. 1555, the Portuguese declared war on Rani Abbakka. She emerged victorious in this battle. Later, in A.D. 1568, the Portuguese, under the leadership of Viceroy António de Noronha, invaded Ullal. Rani Abbakka escaped and attacked the Portuguese army with 200 soldiers. General Peixoto was killed in the battle, and several Portuguese soldiers were captured. With the help of Abbakka's husband Lakshmappa Arasa, the Portuguese later defeated Rani Abbakka and imprisoned her. She died in prison.

The role of reformers, the press, and the formation of the Indian National Congress in 1885 helped unite people for the national cause.

It played a crucial role in shaping the Indian Constitution and securing legal rights for marginalized communities.

questions.text: Write about the Poona Pact.
questions.text_as_printed: Write about the Poona Pact. (Difficult)

answer.value: The Poona Pact was signed on September 24, 1932, between Mahatma Gandhi and Dr. B.R. Ambedkar. It was a compromise to resolve the issue of separate electorates for Dalits proposed in the Communal Award. According to the pact, Dalits were granted reserved seats in legislatures but within the general electorate. The agreement helped avoid further division among Indians during the freedom struggle.

questions.text: Explain the Quit India Movement.
questions.text_as_printed: Explain the Quit India Movement. (Difficult)

answer.value: The Quit India Movement was launched on August 8, 1942, by Mahatma Gandhi with the call “Do or Die.” It demanded an immediate end to British rule in India. The British responded with mass arrests of leaders and repression, but people across the country rose in protest. Though it was eventually suppressed, it marked the final major movement before independence and reflected India's readiness for self-rule.

questions.text: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar
questions.text_as_printed: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar (Difficult)

answer.value: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar was a jurist, social reformer, and the chief architect of the Indian Constitution. Born into a Dalit family, he fought against social discrimination and untouchability. He played a vital role in securing legal rights for marginalized communities. Ambedkar was also India's first Law Minister and founded the Republican Party of India. His efforts laid the foundation for social justice and equality in modern India.

questions.text: Subhas Chandra Bose
questions.text_as_printed: Subhas Chandra Bose (Difficult)

answer.value: Subhas Chandra Bose was a prominent freedom fighter and leader of the Indian National Army (INA). He believed in armed struggle against British rule and gave the famous slogan, “Give me blood, and I will give you freedom.” He formed the INA with Japanese support and established the Provisional Government of Free India in 1943. Bose was known as “Netaji” and inspired many with his courage and patriotism. His mysterious death in 1945 remains a subject of debate.
